subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a moderately detailed static model for a hovering pickup truck, roughly 5.2m by 2.0m with about 0.45m ground clearance, keeping it simple without extra joints since the geometry can stay in model space.

Now I'm working out the body shape using an extruded side profile for the cab and hood, with separate boxes for the bed floor and walls, and figuring out the correct cross product orientation so the extrusion thickness runs along the right axis.

Defining cab outline and windows...

I'm thinking through paint schemes - olive drab military mottle versus cyberpunk neon accents - then working out the geometry for side windows and the sloped windshield, calculating the z-coordinates along the slope to position the glass correctly.

I'm confirming the window thickness fits within the body half-width, then picking a dark tinted glass color instead of a bright glow. Now I'm working out the windshield geometry as a thin angled box following the slope direction from the hood to the cab.

Now I'm adding military details like a hood plate with neon stripes, a pintle-mounted gun turret, rocket pod, and bed accessories like ammo crates and a roll bar. Then I'm working out the hover thruster pods at the four corners, lathed cylindrical nacelles with glowing downward-facing discs and struts connecting them to the chassis.

Shaping thruster pod profile...

Adding strut rods connecting pods to the body, then planning texture decals: an emblem on doors, hazard stripes on the bumper, a license plate, a neon kanji sign on the bed side, and camo paint patches, keeping each as outward-facing plane parts.

For lighting, I'm adding glowing headlight boxes near the front bumper and a magenta cyberpunk light bar up front, with the rear plate facing backward and transparent SVG textures for the decals.

Now I'm working out an armored front bumper with hazard-stripe texturing on a forward-facing plane, cyan underglow strips along the sides, hover skirts instead of wheels, bull bar rods, a slitted grille, and a roof rack with a rocket pod mounted on top.

I'm also designing the roof details with antennas and a searchlight, then building out the truck bed: side wall boxes, a tailgate, a mounted turret with pedestal and barrels, and roll-bar uprights with a crossbar.

For the gun placement I need to check clearance against the cab roof -- raising the pedestal and angling the barrels higher so they clear the roofline while still pointing forward.

Rather than rocket pods on the hood, I'm deciding to skip them and instead add missile launcher boxes mounted on the bed's side rails, flanking the central gun, each tilted upward and forward.

Defining helper functions for parts...

Actually, I'm reconsidering whether to add a joint hierarchy—a root "chassis" joint with child thruster joints at each pod, so the parts can inherit bone orientation for animation purposes rather than relying on static placement alone.

Now I'm thinking through the glow effect import path and settling on the color palette: an olive military base, dark trim, and neon cyan, magenta, and yellow accents for the glow elements.

Setting up the builder for a hover pickup vehicle, defining chassis and thruster joints with left/right naming conventions, then starting the body extrusion with the profile and bevel settings.

Now I'm adding the underbody details: a dark underbody box, neon cyan skirt strips along the sides, a magenta underglow panel, and fender-style armor plates flanking the body.

I'm positioning hover pods at the rear and sides with pylon rods connecting them to the body underside, plus wing-shaped fender plates for armor detailing.

Still working out the pod and wing geometry, adjusting heights and positions so the thruster pods sit properly under the wing plates with enough clearance for the pylons connecting them.

Adding blade geometry for the turbine fans with rotated thin boxes, plus a cyan glow ring band around the pod exterior using a thin lathe shape.

Now I'm working on cab details: a tinted windshield with wipers, door seams made from thin dark boxes to suggest panel lines, a door handle, and side mirrors with simple rod arms.

Shifting to the front end, I'm placing glowing headlight boxes near the hood with a white-cyan tint, a dark grille box with magenta glowing slits, and a lower bumper box, adjusting their vertical positions so they don't overlap awkwardly with the headlights.

Adding a hazard plane and a magenta/cyan light bar along the cab roof, then working out the hood's sloped surface geometry so I can run thin neon stripe boxes along it.

Positioning the box with correct axis and tilt direction, then moving on to decals: a door emblem plane placed in the door panel region below the windows, plus a rear gate label and neon sign plane positioned on the bed wall's outer face.

Now I'm sketching the actual texture art — a star emblem with a stroked circle and cyan accent, a hazard-stripe pattern built from diagonal yellow/black polygons, a monospace license plate reading "NX-7734" with a cyan border, and starting on the neon sign text.

Since custom fonts likely won't render reliably, I'll fall back to simple ASCII text like "HOVER-OPS" and "ARES" built from basic shapes, plus a launcher face with a 2x3 circle grid. I'm also adding a tailgate graphic with a magenta-and-white glowing skull for character, positioning its plane at the rear of the vehicle and placing a plate below it on the bumper.

Now I'm positioning the rear bumper box and license plate, orienting the plate so it reads correctly from behind, then working out placement for the glowing red taillights near the tailgate edges.

Next I'm building the gun mount: a pedestal cylinder rising from the truck bed, a mount head box on top, and twin barrel rods extending forward from it.

Checking the gun shield position against the barrel geometry to make sure they don't improperly intersect, then adding a floor ring for the pedestal base and placing a roll bar with uprights near the gun mount.

Now I'm positioning the crossbar and checking clearance with the barrels above it, adding floodlight glow boxes on the crossbar, and placing rear antenna rods with glowing colored tips. I'm also starting to lay out cargo crates on the truck bed.

I'm adding a glowing cyan energy cell cylinder near the crates, skipping rocket launchers to save space, and working out armor plate panels on the doors while avoiding collision with the emblem placement.

Now I'm sizing and positioning the emblem to sit properly above the armor plate without overlapping the door window, then adding a sensor dome and radar dish on the cab roof instead of hood-mounted pods for the military look.

I'm considering rear spoiler fins and canard wings for the tail but deciding to skip them as unnecessary, moving on to finalize the window color.

Now I'm deciding against adding visible interior seats since the windows will be opaque, and tallying parts at around 150, which fits under the line budget. I'm starting to write a helper function for building box-shaped parts attached to the chassis bone.

Still writing helper functions...

Adding struts between pod tops and the body side walls to connect them structurally, keeping pod caps bound to their own pod joints while the braces attach to the chassis, and now sorting out how the wings should sit relative to the body's bottom edge.

Positioning the front and rear wings symmetrically along the z-axis with trapezoid neon edge strips running along their outer tips, confirming the camo extrusion and the lathe floor start at y=0, and typing the profile outline array correctly for TypeScript before moving into the SVG texture strings.

Writing emblem SVG...

Now I'm designing a license plate with a dark background, cyan border, and bold monospace callsign text, then sketching a skull icon using layered ellipses for the head and jaw, dark eyes, a nose triangle, and magenta glowing outlines.

Adding a glowing neon sign texture with chevron accents, then deciding to swap the thruster blade boxes for a proper fan disc graphic—dark circle base with radiating cyan-gradient blade wedges for a glowing spinning-fan look.

Adding more car details...

Writing camo and hull paint logic...
